story.what_it_does: Supreme Industries is a plastic pipes and products maker, described as India's largest plastics processor. It sells piping, plus value-added products such as CPVC pipes, furniture, industrial components and, newly, windows and doors. It reports being debt free with a cash surplus of ₹685 crore at 30 Sep 2026.
story.plans: Management plans about ₹1,000 crore of capex for FY2026-27 (the Sep-26 call later lowered the FY27 figure to ₹700 crore), funded from internal accruals. The aim is to lift capacity to 1.5 million MT by 2027-28, with Jammu and Patna units expected in 2026-27. Management also plans new windows and doors capacity and a cross laminated product launch.
story.moat: The notes point to scale and financial strength: a 13% piping market share, an ROCE of about 25% over 18 years, zero debt and low receivable days. The Wavin business adds customers and capacity. The notes do not describe patents or other formal barriers, and raw material prices follow crude oil, which management does not control.

scenarios.story: Volumes recover as polymer prices settle, and the October pickup (about 23% growth in the first 25 days) carries through the rest of the year. New capacity and value-added products then add to sales while margins stay near the 14% guidance.
signals_to_watch: Plastic piping volume growth versus the cut guidance of 13% for FY27
Volume growth in the months after the first 25 days of October (23%)

scenarios.story: A weak first half is followed by a gradual recovery, so full-year volume growth lands near the lowered guidance of about 10% overall. Margins hold around 14% and the company stays debt free while spending on its capex plan.
signals_to_watch: Company-wide volume growth guidance of 10% for FY27
Operating margin guidance of 14% for FY27

scenarios.story: Polymer price swings keep disrupting distribution and channel inventory, and the recovery fades. Guidance has already been cut once, and the notes say margins missed estimates two quarters running.
signals_to_watch: Whether H1 volume growth of only 1% improves
